Work done = Time × Efficiency

Time ∝ 1/Efficiency

**Calculation:**

In one hour,

Pipe 1 can fill 1/5

Pipe 2 can fill 1/7 

Pipe 3 can empty 1/14 

In one hour all the pipes can fill 1/5 + 1/7 - 1/14

⇒ The tank will be filled completely in 70/19 = 3(13)/(19) hours

**∴ 3(13)/(19) hours will it take to fill the tank completely**

questions.question: The side length of a rhombus is √5 cm and its area is 4 cm². What will be the sum of the lengths of its diagonals?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the rhombus, (a) = √5 cm

Area of rhombus, (A) = 4 cm²

A = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

By Pythagoras theorem - 4a² = d1² + d₂²

**Calculation:**

According to the question

A = 1/2 × d1 × d₂

⇒ 2A = d₁d₂

Now,

(d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = 4a² + 2 × 2A

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = 4a² + 4A

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = 4 × (√5)² + 4 × 4

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = (4 × 5 + 16)

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = (20 + 16)

⇒ (d1 + d2)² = 36

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = 6 cm

**∴ The sum of the length of the diagonals is 6 cm**

 KE = (1)/(2)m{v²}

therefore KE = (1)/(2)frac{{{p²}}}{m}

velocity = 5 ms-1

⇒ BC² = (25 – 16)

⇒ BC² = 9

⇒ BC = 3 m

Again,

In ΔEDC

By pythagoras theorem

CD² = EC² – ED²

⇒ CD² = (5)² – (3)²

Now,

BD = BC + CD

⇒ BD = (3 + 4) M

⇒ BD = 7 m

**∴ The width of the road is 7 m**

• In other words, in one minute, the minute hand gains 5 {1 over 2}º more than hour hand.
 
• In one hour the gain will be = 5 {1 over 2}º × 60 = 330º
 
• In other words, the minute hand will gain [ 330/6 = 55] 55 minutes to the hour hand. or the minute hand moves by 55 minutes in an hour.

Hence, '55' is the correct answer.
